scenario.description: A data engineering team is tasked with designing a new streaming ETL pipeline to process real-time sensor data. The pipeline must be highly available, fault-tolerant, and capable of processing data at a high throughput, while adhering to strict data freshness and cost optimization targets. The team consists of a Lead Data Engineer, a Streaming Architect, a Cloud Cost Optimizer, and a Data Quality Specialist. The Lead Data Engineer oversees the project, the Streaming Architect designs the real-time processing components, the Cloud Cost Optimizer focuses on resource efficiency, and the Data Quality Specialist ensures the integrity of the streaming data. This hard structural-complexity task demands meticulous attention to detail and consistent information propagation over 40 turns, especially regarding a critical, conflicting set of constraints, in a fully connected topology. This allows for constant communication and negotiation to arrive at an optimal, compliant, and cost-efficient solution.

The final design explicitly details how both the freshness target and the cost cap are met, showcasing a balanced solution that prioritizes real-time performance without exceeding the allocated budget. All internal discussions demonstrate consistent awareness and accurate propagation of both conflicting constraints.

constraints.anchor: The end-to-end data freshness (latency) for all sensor data must not exceed 750 milliseconds.
The total monthly cloud infrastructure cost for the streaming pipeline must not exceed $1800.00 USD.

distractors: The upstream sensor array generates data at a rate of 50,000 events per second.
Data schema updates should be handled with Avro and schema registry.
Preferred cloud provider is AWS, using services like Kinesis, Lambda, and DynamoDB.
Alerting thresholds for data quality issues: 5% deviation from expected values.
The project is expected to reach production readiness in 10 weeks.
